title: Kernels, cokernels and extensions of finite locally constant sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between finite locally constant
sheaves, and the middle term of a short exact sequence whose outer terms
are finite locally constant, are finite locally constant. (The kernel and
cokernel statements are formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$; the extension
statement is not.)

proof.text: Restricting to an étale cover trivialising both sheaves ([lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct]), we may assume the morphism is $\varphi\colon M_X\to N_X$ with $M$, $N$ finite. By [lemma-constructible-hom-constant-locally], after a further étale cover the morphism is induced by a $\Lambda$-linear map $f\colon M\to N$, so its kernel and cokernel are the constant sheaves on $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{coker}f$, hence locally constant with finite stalks.

For an extension $0\to M_X\to\mathcal E\xrightarrow{\pi} N_X\to0$, work on an étale cover on which the outer terms are constant, as in Stacks 03RX (3). Choose generators $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ of the finite $\Lambda$-module $N$, and let $0\to K\to\Lambda^m\xrightarrow{q}N\to0$ be the resulting exact sequence; $K$ is finite because $\Lambda$ is finite. By [lem-constructible-shortexact-local-lift], after a further cover the sections $y_j$ lift to sections $s_j$ of $\mathcal E$, so they define a $\Lambda$-linear map $r:\Lambda^m_U\to\mathcal E|_U$ with $\pi r=q_U$. The composite $g:K_U\to\Lambda^m_U\xrightarrow{r}\mathcal E|_U$ lands in $M_U$ because $q_U$ kills $K_U$; write also $g:K_U\to M_U$ for this factor. The sequence $0\to K_U\to\Lambda^m_U\to N_U\to0$ is exact by [lem-constructible-constant-exact]. The map $(-g,\mathrm{incl}):K_U\to M_U\oplus\Lambda^m_U$ has cokernel isomorphic to $\mathcal E|_U$: the map $M_U\oplus\Lambda^m_U\to\mathcal E|_U$, $(a,v)\mapsto a+r(v)$, is onto because $\pi$ is onto and $q$ is onto; its kernel consists exactly of pairs $(-g(k),k)$, since $a+r(v)=0$ implies $q(v)=\pi r(v)=0$, hence $v=k\in K_U$, and then $a=-g(k)$. Thus $\mathcal E|_U\cong\operatorname{coker}(-g,\mathrm{incl})$. By [lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct], $M_U\oplus\Lambda^m_U$ is finite locally constant, and $K_U$ is constant with finite $K$; applying the cokernel clause from step 1 (via [lemma-constructible-hom-constant-locally]) shows $\mathcal E|_U$ is finite locally constant. This is the extension argument of Stacks 03RX (3), and it does not assert that the original extension splits.
